reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning with external explainability tools to ensure both domain-aware insights and data-driven attributions. Autonomous analysis helps identify intuitive feature-level changes based on known socioeconomic patterns, while XAI tools provide rigorous, model-agnostic feature importance scores to validate and prioritize impactful modifications. This combination increases the likelihood of discovering actionable, realistic counterfactuals that flip the prediction.

autonomous_tasks.query: What socioeconomic or demographic features are most likely to increase the probability of predicting >50K in the adult income dataset?
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of features and suggested changes (e.g., higher education level, higher age, higher work class) that are known to correlate with higher income in real-world data

autonomous_tasks.query: Compare the current input features to known benchmarks where income >50K is common (e.g., high education-num, high age, occupation of tech or executive roles), and identify the most plausible changes to flip the prediction.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A set of specific feature-value pairs that align with known income-increasing trends

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides a game-theoretic interpretation of feature contributions, identifying which features most influence the class margin between <=50K and >50K. LIME offers local interpretability by approximating the model with an interpretable model, revealing local patterns. Integrated Gradients help quantify the effect of each feature moving from zero to the current value, providing a smooth gradient-based attribution. Sensitivity Analysis directly measures how much the prediction shifts when a feature is perturbed, ensuring that changes actually lead to the target class. Together, these tools validate and prioritize counterfactual changes with high confidence.
